To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the value of digital health data is enormous but the process for extracting and refining that value is complex, and the resulting products will be distributed through the private sector.

the value of digital health data will increase substantially as the information is refined into software algorithms, and that private industry will play a major role in creating and distributing these new digital products, which will be sold to clinicians, patients, health systems, and payers.
the growing store of electronic health data has unique attributes and that the exploitation of this resource must be managed to ensure that all stakeholders are treated fairly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the value of the data that clinicians create every day in caring for patients, and with the process of transforming those data into useful products.
how we can best use the data that are being created by clinicians and patients in their daily interactions to improve care for all patients.
the development of new clinical products that will be based on the growing store of digitized health data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

digital health data are a new resource, the exploitation of which will create enormous benefits for society but that will be accompanied by risks for the patients who contribute their data and for clinicians who create and share them.
the exploitation of the digital health resource is inevitable.

the exploitation of the vast pool of electronic clinical data is a complex and challenging undertaking that will require a new approach to the development and regulation of the new products that will emerge from it.

it has been a very positive experience.
the digital health economy is a new frontier that will require new rules, but the opportunities it creates will be enormous.
the digital health economy is a work in progress, but one that is moving quickly.

the digital health economy is here to stay.
clinicians are creating a new resource that has enormous potential to improve health and health care.
the digital health economy is coming.
